title: Parade from the cutoff to Algiers through open fields
summary: He recalls a Labor Day parade walked from the cutoff to Algiers, played to cows and horses.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: And you know, do you know this? You're playing your horn, walking on the road like that. Do you know your inside be dry as anything? Look like you make your throat be dry. Now that happened to us one time. From the cutoff. You ever been going down to the cutoff? Down on the other side. Yeah. We played, I believe you was that son, we played at the parade.
We played down there, walked from the cutoff to Algiers, man.
Man, I said, no more job like that. See, coming up. Man, it looked like we don't get to town.
I'm on Labor Day. That's right, that's right.

And so, I told him, I said, man, no more. Was he going back down there? I swear, Bill, we got down there so fast. I know how we got down there. Looked like we used to fly down there. Going back, we made it fast. And do you know we didn't know we got down there so fast? We coming up here? Didn't he? You know, that's what we were playing for. The horses and the cows in the field. The horses was dancing with one another. I didn't know that one was over there. Yeah, you know what?
I didn't know that one was over there.
The horses dancing. Horses and cows running for one another. Yeah, really?

And I said, now, I didn't give no credit on there. What they could have done is hire the truck to bring us up there and bring us back down there. We were playing a little longer down there. And we get down there. We had to play down there in a big open field for them. Playing. All you're playing for the cows and the mules and horses and dogs.
You didn't see nothing in life.

Did you see anything? All you're seeing land, you understand, like pasture and all that. I said, man, if I knew it was going to be like that, I'd never come on no job like that. And I made a promise. I said, go on, I'm going to play music. If I know a job going to be something like that, you don't have no more trouble. You need to go on with them kind of jobs. And that's the hardest thing that's playing for you. You don't have nobody. Do you know you'll be more tired than you'll be working? See? And just like this gallip boy played this year. See, this year's the reason they don't want it out and give them no punishment. They blocked up all the traffic.
